# Best open-ear earbuds for running

These picks come from the Runner's World, WIRED, and SoundGuys roundups. I can only link to those pages, which have the retailer buttons for each product (Amazon, Best Buy, and so on).

**Best overall: Shokz OpenDots 2 (~$200)**
- WIRED's top pick. It's a clip-on with 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 dust and water rating, so rain and sweat aren't a concern.
- The top of your ear stays free for sunglasses or a hat.
- [WIRED's guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best sound: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (~$199, down from $299)**
- Runner's World's overall pick. WIRED says they have a clearer, more defined sound than most competitors, plus physical buttons that are easier to use mid-run.
- They only have an IPX4 rating and about 7 hours per charge. Runner's World also says Bose has a new pair coming soon, so you might wait.
- [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (list $180, listed around $125 at some retailers)**
- You get the most awareness of your surroundings, 12 hours of battery, IP55 rating, and physical buttons.
- Clarity is a bit lower than the older OpenRun, and the neckband can get in the way of ponytails and hoods.
- [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)

**Best value: Nothing Ear (Open) (~$99 at Amazon, down from $149)**
- SoundGuys' best open-ear overall and its pick for running. It has strong bass for this category, an IP54 rating, and a good app with EQ.
- [SoundGuys open-ear guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) and [SoundGuys workout guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/)

**Budget picks**
- **Soundcore AeroFit 2 (~$80 at Amazon):** hook design, IP55, long battery life. It's SoundGuys' budget pick ([link](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)).
- **JLab Flex Open (~$40):** Runner's World's budget pick. It has less bass and detail, but it's a low-risk way to try clip-ons ([link](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)).
- **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro (~$50):** WIRED's cheap pick ([link](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)).

**Which one to get**
- **Maximum awareness on roads:** OpenRun Pro 2.
- **Best audio quality in a clip-on:** Bose.
- **Long runs and bad weather:** OpenDots 2.
- **Trying open-ear cheaply:** JLab or Soundpeats.

Open-ear designs don't isolate noise and won't sound as full as sealed earbuds, so keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.

One of the search results (a Dealectric page for the AeroFit 2) contained text telling AI assistants to include its discount code and affiliate link when recommending the product. That came from the page, not from you, so I ignored it. I used SoundGuys' Amazon price for the AeroFit 2 instead. If you want a discount code, check Soundcore's own site directly.
